title: Closing the First Light dialog mid-capture orphans the exposure, and there is no cancel inside the dialog
what_happened: While the dialog showed 'Working on it... / Capturing exposure' with an indeterminate bar, it offered NO cancel or abort - only the title-bar X. Clicking the X closed the dialog but did NOT stop the exposure: navigating to Imaging showed 'Exposing... 999858.8s remaining' with the camera locked. The Imaging viewer's 'Abort capture' X was then clicked three times (tooltip 'Abort capture' confirmed showing, button highlighted) over ~90 seconds and the countdown kept running (999828.7 -> 999816.7 -> 999800.7 -> 999766.7); no abort request appears anywhere in the native log. The camera stayed unusable.
expected: Dismissing a modal that owns a device operation must either abort the operation or refuse to close while it is in flight. And the working state needs a Cancel button of its own - a progress dialog with only an X, where the X does not cancel, is the shape that costs people a night.
repro: Settings > Help & Tutorials > 'Capture your first light' > Start > set exposure to 999999 > Start capture > wait for 'Working on it...' > click the X in the dialog title bar > sidebar Imaging. Observe the running countdown, then click the X at the right of the image toolbar (tooltip 'Abort capture') repeatedly.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-52-working.png (progress state: no Cancel, only the title X); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-53-orphan.png ('Exposing... 999858.8s remaining' after the dialog was closed); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsw-54-abort.png (the 'Abort capture' tooltip visible on the highlighted X while the counter still reads 999800.7s).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/first_light/first_light_flow_dialog.dart (no onDismiss abort, no cancel action in the running state). The dead 'Abort capture' is in the imaging viewer toolbar and does not own the first-light capture path.
proposed_fix: Give the running state a Cancel button that calls the camera abort, and make the dialog's dismiss handler abort as well (or set barrierDismissible/canPop false while a capture is in flight). Separately, route the imaging viewer's abort at the camera rather than at the imaging capture controller so it can stop any in-flight exposure.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end, plus the control experiment the original finding did not run. (1) Running state has no cancel: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-13-working.png shows 'Working on it... / Capturing exposure' with an indeterminate bar and only the title-bar X; code agrees -- first_light_flow_dialog.dart:112-119, _actionsFor returns null for exposing/stretching/solving/annotating. (2) The X closes it mid-run: clicked it, dialog gone (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-15-afterx.png), no new native log lines, and Imaging still read 'Exposing... 999938.8s remaining'. (3) The Imaging 'Abort capture' X is genuinely dead for this path, not merely silent -- this is the part I proved rather than assumed. I hovered to confirm the target (tooltip beginning 'Abo', button highlighted, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-19-tooltip.png), clicked it twice; the counter ran on 999938.8 -> 999912.8 (999999 - 87.2s elapsed, recomputed) and the log gained ZERO lines. I then restarted the app, reconnected the camera, took a 120 s Snapshot FROM the Imaging screen and clicked the same X: the log immediately printed '2026-08-02T16:10:15.432291Z INFO Exposure cancelled'. So a working abort does log, and the first-light abort never reached the backend. Root cause is exactly where the finding points: imaging_screen_actions.dart:273 _abortCapture early-returns on 'if (!_isSingleCapture && !_isLooping) return;' -- imaging-screen-local flags a first-light capture never sets -- while imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:97 decides to SHOW the button from the global 'exposureProgress.remaining > 0'. The same guard means that button is offered and dead for any exposure the Imaging screen did not itself start (sequencer runs, centering); I did not drive those, so treat that as a code-level observation only. (4) Camera stayed unusable: clicking Snapshot during the orphan produced no log line and no new exposure; only killing and restarting the process cleared it. PRECISION CORRECTION for the fixer: the finding implies the modal is freely dismissible, but it is not -- first_light_flow_dialog.dart:61 wraps it in PopScope(canPop: !state.isRunning) and I verified Escape is blocked mid-run (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-14-esc.png, dialog still up). The single hole is the header close button: SkotiqDialog gates it on 'closeEnabled' (skotiq_dialog.dart:89, default true) and calls Navigator.pop directly (skotiq_dialog.dart:98-105), which PopScope does not intercept; FirstLightFlowDialog never passes closeEnabled. So the minimal fix is 'closeEnabled: !state.isRunning' plus a real cancel -- and a real cancel needs a cancel path that does not exist yet: FirstLightOrchestrator.run and firstLightControllerProvider have no cancel/abort token at all (only reset(), first_light_provider.dart:38, which clears UI state while the exposure keeps running). Severity P1 confirmed, not raised: the app-restart recovery keeps it out of P0, but a progress modal whose only exit does not cancel, backed by a device-abort button that lies, is the shape that costs a night.
